claim: African trypanosomes replicate within infected mammals where they are exposed to the complement system.
source: African trypanosomes replicate within infected mammals where they are exposed to the complement system.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about trypanosome biology and their exposure to host immune systems.

claim: The complement system centres around complement C3, which is present in a soluble form in serum but becomes covalently deposited onto the surfaces of pathogens after proteolytic cleavage to C3b.
source: This system centres around complement C3, which is present in a soluble form in serum but becomes covalently deposited onto the surfaces of pathogens after proteolytic cleavage to C3b.
evidence: This describes established mechanisms of the complement system.

claim: Membrane-associated C3b triggers different complement-mediated effectors which promote pathogen clearance.
source: Membrane-associated C3b triggers different complement-mediated effectors which promote pathogen clearance.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about complement function.

claim: African trypanosomes have a cell surface receptor, ISG65, which binds to C3b.
source: To counter complement-mediated clearance, African trypanosomes have a cell surface receptor, ISG65, which binds to C3b and which decreases the rate of trypanosome clearance in an infection model.
evidence: This is supported by previous research cited in the manuscript.

claim: ISG65 decreases the rate of trypanosome clearance in an infection model.
source: To counter complement-mediated clearance, African trypanosomes have a cell surface receptor, ISG65, which binds to C3b and which decreases the rate of trypanosome clearance in an infection model.
evidence: This is supported by previous experimental work referenced in the manuscript.

claim: ISG65 has two distinct binding sites for C3b.
source: We reveal through cryogenic electron microscopy that ISG65 has two distinct binding sites for C3b, only one of which is available in C3 and C3d.
evidence: This is directly supported by the cryo-EM structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Only one of the two ISG65 binding sites for C3b is available in C3 and C3d.
source: We reveal through cryogenic electron microscopy that ISG65 has two distinct binding sites for C3b, only one of which is available in C3 and C3d.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: ISG65 does not block the formation of C3b.
source: We show that ISG65 does not block the formation of C3b or the function of the C3 convertase which catalyses the surface deposition of C3b.
evidence: This is supported by experimental assays described in the manuscript.

claim: ISG65 does not block the function of the C3 convertase which catalyses the surface deposition of C3b.
source: We show that ISG65 does not block the formation of C3b or the function of the C3 convertase which catalyses the surface deposition of C3b.
evidence: This is supported by C3 convertase activity assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: ISG65 forms a specific conjugate with C3b.
source: However, we show that ISG65 forms a specific conjugate with C3b, perhaps acting as a decoy.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing conjugate formation.

claim: ISG65 may act as a decoy by forming a conjugate with C3b.
source: However, we show that ISG65 forms a specific conjugate with C3b, perhaps acting as a decoy.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the conjugate formation data.

claim: ISG65 occludes the binding sites for complement receptors 2 and 3.
source: ISG65 also occludes the binding sites for complement receptors 2 and 3, which may disrupt recruitment of immune cells, including B cells, phagocytes, and granulocytes.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison with known CR2 and CR3 binding sites.

claim: Occlusion of CR2 and CR3 binding sites by ISG65 may disrupt recruitment of immune cells, including B cells, phagocytes, and granulocytes.
source: ISG65 also occludes the binding sites for complement receptors 2 and 3, which may disrupt recruitment of immune cells, including B cells, phagocytes, and granulocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known functions of CR2 and CR3.

claim: ISG65 protects trypanosomes by combining multiple approaches to dampen the complement cascade.
source: This suggests that ISG65 protects trypanosomes by combining multiple approaches to dampen the complement cascade.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings in the manuscript.

claim: African trypanosomes can survive in the blood and tissue spaces of mammals for decades.
source: African trypanosomes can survive in the blood and tissue spaces of mammals for decades (Sudarshi et al., 2014), despite constant exposure to the molecules and cells of the immune system.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Trypanosomes have evolved a unique surface coat packed with many copies of a single variant surface glycoprotein (VSG).
source: They have evolved a unique surface coat packed with many copies of a single variant surface glycoprotein (VSG) (Schwede et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Antigenically distinct VSGs are expressed over the course of an infection at a population level, thereby preventing antibody-mediated clearance.
source: At a population level, antigenically distinct VSGs are expressed over the course of an infection, thereby preventing antibody-mediated clearance (Schwede and Carrington, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Recent studies have identified receptors which function within the trypanosome surface coat and which bind to either complement factor C3b or complement modulator factor H.
source: Recent studies have identified receptors which function within the trypanosome surface coat and which bind to either complement factor C3b (Macleod et al., 2022) or complement modulator factor H (Macleod et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: ISG65 was identified as the trypanosome C3b receptor.
source: ISG65 was identified as the trypanosome C3b receptor and has been shown to reduce the susceptibility of trypanosomes to antibody-mediated clearance in a mouse infection model (Macleod et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: ISG65 has been shown to reduce the susceptibility of trypanosomes to antibody-mediated clearance in a mouse infection model.
source: ISG65 was identified as the trypanosome C3b receptor and has been shown to reduce the susceptibility of trypanosomes to antibody-mediated clearance in a mouse infection model (Macleod et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous experimental work.

claim: The complement system involves a complex set of molecular cascades.
source: The complement system involves a complex set of molecular cascades (Gros et al., 2008; Zipfel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The complement cascades come together at the conversion of serum complement C3 into C3b and the deposition of C3b on a pathogen surface through the formation of a thioester bond between the TED domain of C3b and cell surface components.
source: These come together at the conversion of serum complement C3 into C3b and the deposition of C3b on a pathogen surface through the formation of a thioester bond between the TED domain of C3b and cell surface components (Ricklin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: C3b deposition can occur through three major and distinct pathways: classical, lectin, and alternative.
source: C3b deposition can occur through three major and distinct pathways.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the complement system.

claim: In the classical pathway, antibodies mediate the recruitment of C3b.
source: In the classical pathway, antibodies mediate the recruitment of C3b, while in the lectin pathway, this results from the recognition of cell surface glycans.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the complement system.

claim: In the lectin pathway, C3b recruitment results from the recognition of cell surface glycans.
source: In the classical pathway, antibodies mediate the recruitment of C3b, while in the lectin pathway, this results from the recognition of cell surface glycans.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the complement system.

claim: In the classical and lectin pathways, C4bC2b convertases are established which catalyse the conversion of C3 into C3b and its surface deposition.
source: In both cases, these events establish C4bC2b convertases, which catalyse the conversion of C3 into C3b and its surface deposition.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the complement system.

claim: The alternative pathway involves stochastic conversion of C3 into C3b, resulting in an initial deposition event independent of other molecular recognition processes.
source: In contrast, the alternative pathway involves stochastic conversion of C3 into C3b, resulting in an initial deposition event independent of other molecular recognition processes (Nilsson and Nilsson Ekdahl, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The first deposited C3b molecules can assemble with factors B and D, leading to formation of the C3 convertase, C3bBb.
source: The first deposited C3b molecules can then assemble with factors B and D, leading to formation of the C3 convertase, C3bBb, which catalyses deposition of further C3b molecules and amplification of downstream responses (Rooijakkers et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The C3bBb convertase catalyses deposition of further C3b molecules and amplification of downstream responses.
source: The first deposited C3b molecules can then assemble with factors B and D, leading to formation of the C3 convertase, C3bBb, which catalyses deposition of further C3b molecules and amplification of downstream responses (Rooijakkers et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Direct recognition of immobilised C3b, or its cleavage products iC3b, C3dg, and C3d, by complement receptors stimulates the activity of various immune cells.
source: Direct recognition of immobilised C3b, or its cleavage products iC3b, C3dg, and C3d, by complement receptors stimulates the activity of various immune cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about complement receptor function.

claim: Complement receptor 1 (CR1) is found on macrophages.
source: Complement receptor 1 (CR1) is found on macrophages and binding of CR1 to C3b promotes phagocytosis of pathogens such as Leishmania (Rosenthal et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Binding of CR1 to C3b promotes phagocytosis of pathogens such as Leishmania.
source: Complement receptor 1 (CR1) is found on macrophages and binding of CR1 to C3b promotes phagocytosis of pathogens such as Leishmania (Rosenthal et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Complement receptor 2 (CR2) is found on B cells and forms a signal-transducing B cell co-receptor with CD19 and CD81.
source: Complement receptor 2 (CR2) is found on B cells and forms a signal-transducing B cell co-receptor with CD19 and CD81 (Bradbury et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: CR2-CD19-CD81 is stimulated upon binding to C3d.
source: CR2-CD19-CD81 is stimulated upon binding to C3d, and the absence of CR2 severely attenuates humoral immunity (Fischer et al., 1998; Croix et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The absence of CR2 severely attenuates humoral immunity.
source: CR2-CD19-CD81 is stimulated upon binding to C3d, and the absence of CR2 severely attenuates humoral immunity (Fischer et al., 1998; Croix et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Complement receptors 3 and 4 are integrins found on various leukocytes.
source: Complement receptors 3 and 4 are integrins found on various leukocytes and are associated with diverse effects, such as enhancement of natural killer cell cytotoxicity and antibody-dependent eosinophil cytotoxicity against schistosomes (Erdei et al., 2019; Capron et al., 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CR3 and CR4 are associated with diverse effects, such as enhancement of natural killer cell cytotoxicity and antibody-dependent eosinophil cytotoxicity against schistosomes.
source: Complement receptors 3 and 4 are integrins found on various leukocytes and are associated with diverse effects, such as enhancement of natural killer cell cytotoxicity and antibody-dependent eosinophil cytotoxicity against schistosomes (Erdei et al., 2019; Capron et al., 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: C3b can trigger a cascade which leads to recruitment of the pore-forming membrane attack complex.
source: Through mechanisms distinct from those mediated by complement receptors, C3b can trigger a cascade which leads to recruitment of the pore-forming membrane attack complex (Tegla et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Deposited C3b binds to other complement factors, resulting in formation of a C5 convertase.
source: Here, deposited C3b binds to other complement factors, resulting in formation of a C5 convertase.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the complement system.

claim: The C5 convertase cleaves complement factor C5, generating C5b.
source: This cleaves complement factor C5, generating C5b, which recruits factors C6 and C7 to cause membrane association.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the complement system.

claim: C5b recruits factors C6 and C7 to cause membrane association.
source: This cleaves complement factor C5, generating C5b, which recruits factors C6 and C7 to cause membrane association.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the complement system.

claim: Factors C8 and C9 can bind to C5b7 on the pathogen surface, leading to the formation of a pore which mediates cell death.
source: Factors C8 and C9 can then bind to C5b7 on the pathogen surface, leading to the formation of a pore which mediates cell death (Couves et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Pathogens have evolved a wide range of different approaches to evade complement-mediated destruction by regulating different stages of the complement cascade.
source: Pathogens have evolved a wide range of different approaches to evade complement-mediated destruction by regulating different stages of the complement cascade (Zipfel et al., 2013; Lambris et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: S. aureus Efb-C binds to the TED domain of C3 and prevents the conformational change required to generate C3b.
source: These include S. aureus Efb-C which binds to the TED domain of C3 and prevents the conformational change required to generate C3b Hammel et al., 2007;
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: S. aureus Efb, Ehp, and Sbi bind to the TED domain of C3/C3d and prevent binding of complement receptor 2, thereby inhibiting B cell recruitment.
source: S. aureus Efb, Ehp, and Sbi which bind to the TED domain of C3/C3d and prevent binding of complement receptor 2, thereby inhibiting B cell recruitment Ricklin et al., 2008; Isenman et al., 2010;
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Smallpox virus SPICE displaces factor B, preventing C3 convertase function.
source: smallpox virus SPICE which displaces factor B, preventing C3 convertase function Forneris et al., 2010;
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: S. aureus SCIN and Sbi bind to the C3bBb C3 convertase and hold it in an inactive conformation.
source: and S. aureus SCIN and Sbi which bind to the C3bBb C3 convertase and hold it in an inactive conformation (Rooijakkers et al., 2009; Clark et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The crystal structure of ISG65 bound to C3d was previously determined, revealing how the three core helices of ISG65 form a concave surface to which C3d binds.
source: We previously determined the crystal structure of ISG65 bound to C3d (equivalent to the TED domain of C3b), revealing how the three core helices of ISG65 form a concave surface to which C3d binds (Macleod et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: The previous crystal structure of ISG65-C3d does not reveal the full interaction interface between ISG65 and C3b.
source: However, this study also showed that this structure does not reveal the full interaction interface between ISG65 and C3b.
evidence: This is supported by previous experimental data.

claim: Surface plasmon resonance had been used to measure the affinities of ISG65 for the different fragments of C3, C3b, and C3d.
source: Surface plasmon resonance had been used to measure the affinities of ISG65 for the different fragments of C3, C3b, and C3d (Macleod et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: C3b exhibited a higher affinity for ISG65 than C3d, suggesting that ISG65 forms contacts with C3b in addition to those structurally characterised with the TED domain.
source: C3b exhibited a higher affinity for C3b than C3d, suggesting that ISG65 forms contacts with C3b in addition to those structurally characterised with the TED domain.
evidence: This is an inference based on affinity measurements from previous research.

claim: Fluorinated octyl maltoside improved particle distribution in grids while avoiding dissociation of the ISG65-C3b complex.
source: We prepared ISG65-C3b complex in the presence of fluorinated octyl maltoside, which improved particle distribution in grids while avoiding dissociation of the complex.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations during sample preparation.

claim: 14,339 movies were collected from which particles were extracted and a three-dimensional volume was calculated.
source: We collected 14,339 movies from which particles were extracted and a three-dimensional volume was calculated.
evidence: This describes the experimental data collection.

claim: Local refinement using a mask covering ISG65 and the TED and CUB domains of C3b resulted in a volume at 3.4 Å resolution.
source: To improve the resolution of the region containing the binding site, local refinement was performed using a mask covering ISG65 and the TED and CUB domains of C3b, resulting in a volume at 3.4 Å resolution.
evidence: This describes the resolution achieved in the cryo-EM analysis.

claim: A molecular model for the ISG65-C3b complex was built guided by previous structures of ISG65 and C3b and by an Alphafold2 model of ISG65.
source: Guided by previous structures of ISG65 (Macleod et al., 2022) and C3b (Janssen et al., 2006) and by an Alphafold2 (Jumper et al., 2021) model of ISG65, we were able to build a molecular model for the ISG65-C3b complex (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the modeling approach using previous structures and computational predictions.

claim: The structure reveals two distinct interfaces formed between ISG65 and C3b.
source: This structure reveals the two distinct interfaces formed between ISG65 and C3b (Figure 1, Figure 2a).
evidence: This is directly supported by the structural data shown in the figures.

claim: Interface 1 between ISG65 and C3b matches that previously identified through crystallographic analysis.
source: The first of these, interface 1, matches that previously identified through our crystallographic analysis (Macleod et al., 2022), with no significant differences between the models in this region.
evidence: This is based on comparison with previous structural data.

claim: Most of loop L2 and parts of loop L3 were ordered and resolved in the cryogenic electron microscopy-derived volume.
source: While our previous structure did not have interpretable electron density for loops L2 and L3, perhaps due to their disorder, or due to proteolysis during crystallisation, most of L2 and parts of L3 were ordered and resolved in our cryogenic electron microscopy-derived volume.
evidence: This describes the improved resolution in the cryo-EM structure compared to the crystal structure.

claim: A de novo model for residues 179–212 of loop L2 was built.
source: This allowed us to build a de novo model for residues 179–212 of L2.
evidence: This describes the modeling of previously unresolved regions.

claim: Loop L2 directly contacts the CUB domain of C3b, with an electrostatic interaction centered around C3b residue Arg954.
source: In particular, L2 directly contacts the CUB domain of C3b, with an electrostatic interaction centered around C3b residue Arg954.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the structural model.

claim: Docking suggests that the second interface does not form between ISG65 and C3.
source: Docking suggests that this second interface does not form between ISG65 and C3, as also seen in a recent structure of ISG65 bound to C3b (Sülzen et al., 2023; Figure 2b).
evidence: This is based on computational docking and comparison with another recent structure.

claim: The presence of the additional contact between ISG65 and C3b, which is not present between ISG65 and the TED domain alone, explains the differences in affinity of ISG65 for C3, C3b, and C3d.
source: The presence of this additional contact between ISG65 and C3b, which is not present between ISG65 and the TED domain alone, explains the differences in affinity of ISG65 for C3, C3b, and C3d.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural and affinity data.

claim: ISG65 binds to immobilised biotinylated C3b with an affinity of 2.9 μM.
source: ISG65 was flowed over immobilised biotinylated C3b and biotinylated C3d, showing binding which fitted a one-to-one binding model with an affinity of 2.9 μM for C3b, and 6 μM for C3d (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on surface plasmon resonance measurements.

claim: ISG65 binds to immobilised biotinylated C3d with an affinity of 6 μM.
source: ISG65 was flowed over immobilised biotinylated C3b and biotinylated C3d, showing binding which fitted a one-to-one binding model with an affinity of 2.9 μM for C3b, and 6 μM for C3d (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on surface plasmon resonance measurements.

claim: The greater affinity of ISG65 for C3b over C3d is attributed to the contacts formed in interface 2.
source: As C3d contains all determinants for formation of interface 1, we attribute the greater affinity for C3b over C3d to the contacts formed in interface 2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural and affinity data.

claim: ISG65ΔL2 and ISG65L2N188A,H189A,Y190A mutations reduced the affinity for C3b to match that for C3d.
source: In neither case did these mutations affect the affinity for C3d but both mutations reduced the affinity for C3b to match that for C3d, supporting the model in which interface 2 forms with C3b but not C3d (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on surface plasmon resonance measurements with mutant proteins.

claim: ISG65ΔL2 and ISG65L2N188A,H189A,Y190A mutations did not affect the affinity for C3d.
source: In neither case did these mutations affect the affinity for C3d but both mutations reduced the affinity for C3b to match that for C3d, supporting the model in which interface 2 forms with C3b but not C3d (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on surface plasmon resonance measurements with mutant proteins.

claim: The same data set yielded a three-dimensional class consisting of a structure of C3b which lacked density for ISG65 and was indistinguishable from previous C3b structures.
source: In addition to determining the structure of C3b bound to ISG65, the same data set also yielded a three-dimensional class consisting of a structure of C3b which lacked density for ISG65 and was indistinguishable from previous C3b structures.
evidence: This describes an additional structure obtained from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The ISG65-bound conformation of C3b is equivalent to the free conformation of C3b.
source: Fitting the model of the C3b-ISG65 complex (without ISG65) into the volume derived for the complex resulted in a map-model correlation of 0.79. When we fitted the same model into the volume derived from C3b alone, the correlation was 0.76, indicating that the ISG65-bound conformation of C3b is equivalent to the free conformation of C3b.
evidence: This is based on comparison of map-model correlations.

claim: Unlike bacterial C3b-effector proteins, such as Efb-C, ISG65 does not prevent C3 from adopting the active conformation of C3b.
source: Therefore, unlike bacterial C3b-effector proteins, such as Efb-C (Hammel et al., 2007), ISG65 does not prevent C3 from adopting the active conformation of C3b.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural comparison and citation to previous work.

claim: ISG65 binding to C3b that is already conjugated to the trypanosome surface is consistent with ISG65 not preventing C3b formation.
source: Indeed, this is consistent with ISG65 binding to C3b that is already conjugated to the trypanosome surface, rather than preventing C3b formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data.

claim: ISG65 does not compete with either factor B or Factor D.
source: In order to determine whether ISG65 can block C3bBb formation, we first compared the ISG65-C3b structure with those of C3b bound to factors B and D30. This indicates that ISG65 does not compete with either factor B or Factor D and does not block the binding of factor B (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison.

claim: ISG65 does not block the binding of factor B.
source: In order to determine whether ISG65 can block C3bBb formation, we first compared the ISG65-C3b structure with those of C3b bound to factors B and D30. This indicates that ISG65 does not compete with either factor B or Factor D and does not block the binding of factor B (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison.

claim: The C3 convertase can form in the presence of ISG65.
source: This suggests that the C3 convertase can form in the presence of ISG65.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural comparison.

claim: When C3 and factor B were mixed with catalytic quantities of C3b and factor D in vitro, this triggered the cleavage of C3 to C3b, as shown by the production of C3a.
source: We, therefore, developed an in vitro assay for C3 convertase formation in which we combined C3 and factor B with catalytic quantities of C3b and factor D. When mixed in vitro, this triggered the cleavage of C3 to C3b, as shown by the production of C3a.
evidence: This describes the results of an in vitro assay.

claim: The in vitro C3 convertase assay resulted in the cleavage of factor B to form Bb and Ba.
source: In addition, it resulted in the cleavage of factor B to form Bb and Ba (Figure 3c).
evidence: This describes the results of an in vitro assay.

claim: When the C3 convertase assay was performed with addition of a greater than threefold excess of ISG65, the production of C3a and Ba were unaltered.
source: When performed with addition of a greater than threefold excess of ISG65, the production of C3a and Ba were unaltered, indicating that formation of the C3bBb C3 convertase can proceed in the presence of ISG65. (Figure 3c).
evidence: This describes the results of an in vitro assay with ISG65.

claim: Formation of the C3bBb C3 convertase can proceed in the presence of ISG65.
source: When performed with addition of a greater than threefold excess of ISG65, the production of C3a and Ba were unaltered, indicating that formation of the C3bBb C3 convertase can proceed in the presence of ISG65. (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro assay results.

claim: Two other recent reports also indicate that ISG65 does not affect formation of the C3 convertase.
source: Indeed, two other recent reports also indicate that ISG65 does not affect formation of the C3 convertase (Sülzen et al., 2023; Lorentzen et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other recent research.

claim: The presence of ISG65 resulted in a high molecular weight band, which was identified through mass spectrometry to be a conjugate of ISG65 with C3b.
source: Comparison of the outcome of C3 convertase formation in the presence and absence of ISG65, revealed that the presence of ISG65 resulted in a high molecular weight band, which we identified through mass spectrometry to be a conjugate of ISG65 with C3b (Figure 3c, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis of the assay products.

claim: When the equivalent experiment was conducted using the same amount of bovine serum albumin instead of ISG65, the formation of the conjugate was not observed.
source: When we conducted the equivalent experiment using the same amount of bovine serum albumin instead of ISG65, we did not observe the formation of this conjugate, suggesting that it occurs specifically due to the proximity of ISG65 and the thioester-forming residue of C3b when in the complex (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is based on a control experiment with BSA.

claim: The ISG65-C3b conjugate occurs specifically due to the proximity of ISG65 and the thioester-forming residue of C3b when in the complex.
source: When we conducted the equivalent experiment using the same amount of bovine serum albumin instead of ISG65, we did not observe the formation of this conjugate, suggesting that it occurs specifically due to the proximity of ISG65 and the thioester-forming residue of C3b when in the complex (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison with the BSA control.

claim: In ISG65 mutants lacking loops L1, L2, or L3, the formation of the ISG65-C3b conjugate was still observed.
source: Finally, to identify which region of ISG65 is responsible for the formation of this conjugate, we used versions of ISG65 which lack loops L1, L2, or L3, or which lacked the flexible C-terminal region (ΔC). In each of the loop mutants, we still observed the formation of the ISG65-C3b conjugate.
evidence: This is based on experiments with ISG65 deletion mutants.

claim: The ISG65-C3b conjugate was not observed in the ΔC mutant lacking the flexible C-terminal region.
source: However, this was not observed in the ΔC mutant (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is based on experiments with ISG65 deletion mutants.

claim: The C-terminal region of ISG65 is an unstructured string of 72 amino acids that does not form part of the binding site for C3b and is not observed in the structures.
source: This C-terminal region is an unstructured string of 72 amino acids that does not form part of the binding site for C3b and is not observed in the structures.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis.

claim: The C-terminal region of ISG65 is predicted to form a flexible linker which connects the structured ISG65 domain to the plasma membrane.
source: It is predicted to form a flexible linker which connects the structured ISG65 domain to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the sequence and structural context.

claim: The proximity of the flexible linker of ISG65 to the thioester site of C3b increases the likelihood of the thioester domain coming into contact with the ISG65 C-terminal linker, leading to the formation of a preferential conjugate between ISG65 and C3b.
source: These data, therefore, suggest that the proximity of the flexible linker of ISG65 to the thioester site of C3b, which occurs due to the interaction of ISG65 with C3/C3b, increases the likelihood of the thioester domain coming into contact with the ISG65 C-terminal linker, leading to the formation of a preferential conjugate between ISG65 and C3b.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutant data and structural context.

claim: ISG65 can interact with C3 before conversion to C3b generates the reactive thioester.
source: Indeed, as ISG65 can interact with C3 before conversion to C3b generates the reactive thioester, this conjugate may be preferred over conjugation of C3b to VSG, acting as a decoy to reduce the conjugation of C3b to other regions of the trypanosome surface.
evidence: This is based on the binding data showing ISG65 can bind C3.

claim: The ISG65-C3b conjugate may be preferred over conjugation of C3b to VSG, acting as a decoy to reduce the conjugation of C3b to other regions of the trypanosome surface.
source: Indeed, as ISG65 can interact with C3 before conversion to C3b generates the reactive thioester, this conjugate may be preferred over conjugation of C3b to VSG, acting as a decoy to reduce the conjugation of C3b to other regions of the trypanosome surface.
